reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a purportedly “100% working” method to claim unlimited free cryptocurrency and directs viewers to enter displayed codes in Binance. It also solicits engagement through a Telegram channel, referral link, and comments containing a Binance Pay ID, creating concrete viewer actions and potential data or referral flows rather than merely discussing a third-party scam.

citations.quote: Stop missing out on free crypto!
Enter the codes shown in this video!
Select Crypto Box or Red Packet.
Comment your Binance Pay ID below for a chance to receive a personal gift!

opening.argument: The description itself places this in a promotional, educational context and expressly warns that cryptocurrency investments carry risk. It also tells viewers to use the official Binance app for security, which is materially different from directing them toward an unverified payment destination. Those qualifications support treating the content as a risky promotional opportunity rather than deceptive solicitation, especially because the materials do not establish that any code produces a reward or that anyone loses money.

citations.quote: Disclaimer: This video is for educational and promotional purposes only.
Cryptocurrency investments carry risk.
Always use the official Binance app to ensure your security

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes “100% working” and instructions to enter codes, but those promotional claims do not override the explicit risk warning and security advice. The description does not establish that a viewer was deceived, paid a fee, surrendered credentials, or received nothing after following the instructions. A claim of possible free crypto can be optimistic or promotional without proving a scam mechanism.

citations.quote: 100% working method to claim unlimited Binance Red Packets and Crypto Box codes
Cryptocurrency investments carry risk

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warnings are generic qualifications, while the central message still presents a “100% working” way to obtain unlimited crypto and tells viewers to enter codes. Advising use of the official app does not verify that the promoted codes work or that the promised benefit exists. The risk disclaimer therefore does not cure the unsupported free-reward representation.

citations.quote: 100% working method to claim unlimited Binance Red Packets and Crypto Box codes
Enter the codes shown in this video!

opening.argument: The material is structured as an operational tutorial: it explains how to open the app, select a feature, and enter a code. The sampled frames show a red-packet code-entry interface, including the prompt to enter a code and an “Open” control. That is consistent with demonstrating an ordinary app workflow for viewers, not proof that the creator is impersonating a service or operating a deceptive scheme. The description also expressly presents the content as educational and promotional.

citations.quote: Open your Binance App.
Tap on the Binance Pay icon.
Select Crypto Box or Red Packet.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the workflow as evidence of a scam, but showing viewers where to select Crypto Box or Red Packet and how to enter a code is precisely the kind of operational instruction an app tutorial would contain. The frames establish an interface and an input process, not deception, unauthorized access, or a fabricated result. External links and engagement requests may be promotional, but they do not change the tutorial format shown here.

citations.quote: Step-by-Step Guide: Perfect for beginners and pro traders alike.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not answer what the tutorial promises. The description says viewers can claim unlimited crypto through a “100% working” method and instructs them to enter the displayed codes. The frames show an input screen and an Open button, but no successful claim, amount, or verification. Thus the operational format supplies a vehicle for the unsupported reward claim rather than neutral education.

citations.quote: 100% working method to claim unlimited Binance Red Packets and Crypto Box codes
Enter the codes shown in this video!

opening.argument: At most, this is an ordinary promotional referral and giveaway-style campaign around an existing red-packet feature. The description invites viewers to join a Telegram channel, follow a Binance Square link, and comment a Binance Pay ID for a chance at a gift. Those are disclosed promotional actions, not evidence of a hidden fee, deposit, guaranteed investment return, or downline-income scheme. The supplied frames show code entry and an Open button, but do not show payment, credentials, or a completed outcome.

citations.quote: Join our Telegram: [https://t.me/Redpocketfreegift] (Daily 100+ Codes!)
Follow on Binance Square: [https://www.binance.com/referral/earn-together/refer2earn-usdc/claim?hl=en-IN&ref=GRO_28502_W90FQ&utm_source=default]
Comment your Binance Pay ID below for a chance to receive a personal gift!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution calls the external channel, referral link, and Pay ID request “concrete” risk flows, but their presence alone does not establish that the channel is malicious, that the link extracts funds, or that the ID is used improperly. The visible workflow is a code-based red-packet promotion. Without evidence of payment, credential harvesting, or a required deposit, the record supports a promotion whose safety and success remain unverified, not a demonstrated scam.

citations.quote: Join our Telegram: [https://t.me/Redpocketfreegift] (Daily 100+ Codes!)
Comment your Binance Pay ID below for a chance to receive a personal gift!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A scam need not demand a deposit or password when it attracts viewers with an allegedly working free-crypto opportunity and sends them toward external engagement and referral paths. The description specifically says the method is “100% working,” promises unlimited codes, and asks for a Binance Pay ID for a possible gift. The absence of a visible fee or completed loss does not establish that the advertised reward is genuine.
